A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FreeKV and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. v3 ends with references and has no appendices; v4 includes Appendices A–F. The complete material supports reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark accuracy in Tables 2–3, inference latency in Figure 7, query-similarity measurements and an efficiency ablation.

after.justification: v4 retains these empirical results and adds InfiniGen comparisons, accuracy ablations, length-scaling experiments, and query-similarity and correction-rate analyses.

M1.justification: Both versions use previous-step KV reuse, min-max page summaries with softmax mean pooling, similarity-triggered head-wise correction, hybrid CPU/GPU layouts and double-buffered recall. v4 evaluates alternatives without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: LongBench v2, LongGenBench, MATH500, AIME24 and GPQA remain the principal datasets, and Figure 1 retains its NIAH and summarization demonstrations. The added analyses use existing task coverage; additional model configurations and sequence-length sweeps change settings.

E2.justification: v4 adds InfiniGen to Tables 2–3 and the latency comparisons in Figures 1 and 7, retaining the existing comparators. Appendix B.1 also evaluates an adapted last-layer-query retrieval alternative. Quest was already absent from v3's efficiency comparison.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include pooling and correction-threshold controls, 16K–128K input and 8K–64K output sweeps, additional model configurations, and correction measurements restricted to finished examples. LongGenBench drops standalone Acc reporting. Existing main-experiment settings are retained, largely relocated to Appendix A.

E4.justification: Appendices B–E add tests of previous-layer versus previous-step retrieval, selection and correction pooling, correction thresholds, sequence-length sensitivity, query-similarity generalization, and correction behavior on unfinished examples. The original system-optimization ablation is retained as Figure 9 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify eight generated samples per reasoning problem and report pass@k and avg@k. Neither adds confidence intervals, significance tests or repeated-run uncertainty estimates. The new correction-rate histograms characterize behavior rather than uncertainty in performance estimates.

E6.justification: Shared accuracy entries in Tables 2–3 remain unchanged, while v4 adds substantial comparator and diagnostic results. Table 4 newly reports AIME24 avg@k of 50.00 for previous-step reuse without correction versus 33.00 for the last-layer alternative; Section 5.3 adds speedups up to 8.5× over InfiniGen. Standalone LongGenBench Acc entries are removed.

T1.justification: The attention/GQA formulation, query-similarity definition, and FreeKV selection and correction equations are unchanged. The added appendices contain empirical comparisons and descriptive metrics, without new formal assumptions, proofs or derivations.

C1.justification: v4 explicitly characterizes FreeKV as training-free in the abstract and introduction. The principal contributions, near-lossless accuracy claim and approximately 13× maximum speedup claim remain unchanged; expanded latency-hiding language largely elaborates the existing contribution.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive explanations of threshold choices, prefill-related scaling limits, generalization across architectures and training stages, and correction behavior on unfinished reasoning examples. Appendix C.2 expands the explanation of why system optimizations enable speculative overlap. Appendix B.3 also introduces a max-pooling correction-cost explanation that is not reconciled with the stated below-threshold correction rule.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-availability link, explicitly mentions scheduling across CPU threads and GPU streams, and documents InfiniGen's group-consistency adaptation and retained skewing-rank configuration. Most Appendix A settings already appeared in v3; their relocation is not new disclosure. Repository availability was not externally verified.

R1.justification: v4 adds InfiniGen and a targeted discussion distinguishing its next-layer re-projection and partial overlap from FreeKV's previous-step reuse and efficient recall. The Chatbot Arena reference is removed. The broader KV-dropping versus KV-retrieval positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: v4 edits prose, integrates appendix references, moves detailed settings and the efficiency-ablation discussion into appendices, and adds acknowledgments and an LLM-usage statement. The main Sections 1–7 retain their order and much of their wording.

P2.justification: Tables 2–3 are transposed into benchmark/metric rows and method columns. Figures 1, 2 and 7 are revised to incorporate InfiniGen, and extensive new ablation tables, heatmaps and correction-rate histograms are added. The original efficiency ablation moves to Appendix C.2 as Figure 9, alongside the conference-format layout change.

improvement.justification: v3 provided limited direct validation of its retrieval, pooling and correction choices. v4 substantially strengthens that foundation through Appendix B's controlled comparisons, broader similarity and correction analyses, and evaluation against the relevant InfiniGen baseline. These gains address important evidential gaps while retaining the original results. They outweigh the loss of standalone LongGenBench Acc reporting and the unresolved max-pooling explanation in Appendix B.3.
